methodologyNotes: Fourteen SDS rotary hammers spanning the two bit systems buyers actually compare in 2026: ten SDS-plus (compact/mid-size, the seed roster) plus four SDS-max additions (Bosch RH540M, Milwaukee 2917-20, Makita HR4013C, Hilti TE 60-ATC-AVR) so the category covers both classes rather than only compacts. Specs re-verified 2026-08-01 directly against manufacturer product pages (Bosch, Milwaukee, DeWalt, Makita, Hilti, Metabo HPT, Ryobi) with independent retailer/distributor corroboration (Ohio Power Tool, Coastal Tool, Platt Electric Supply, CPO Outlets, Beneslast/Benefast, Shell Lumber, Zoro, toolstash.com). Impact energy is reported in joules; where a manufacturer publishes only ft-lbs it is converted at 1 ft-lb = 1.35582 J and rounded to one decimal. blows_per_minute and no_load_rpm are the top of each tool's published variable-speed range (peak, not a fixed value). max_drill_diameter_mm is the tool's own nominal marketing capacity (the inch figure baked into most of these products' names/titles -- e.g. Bosch's own page states GBH18V-26D's 'Max. Capacity in Concrete: 1 in.', Metabo HPT's own model number DH28PFY encodes 28 mm -- converted at 1 in = 25.4 mm and rounded to the nearest mm); it is left null where no manufacturer source ties a single max figure to the model (DeWalt's two compacts publish only an 'optimal drilling range' sub-band, and Hilti's TE-C cordless line doesn't carry an inch-coded name). Prices are the bare-tool (cordless) or full-unit (corded) figure from the manufacturer or a named authorized distributor; several brands (Milwaukee, Hilti) do not publish a public MSRP, so the cited figure is a named distributor's list/contractor price with that caveat carried in priceNote. Corrections made against the seed list: 'Metabo HPT DH28PCY' does not match current US Metabo HPT literature -- DH28PCY/DH28PCY2 only turn up as a legacy 230V/international SKU (Home Depot parts index); the current US 120V model carrying UVP vibration protection is DH28PFY, used here. 'Ryobi PBLRH02' does not exist in any Ryobi catalog, retailer, or manual found; the real 18V ONE+ HP Brushless 1 in. SDS-Plus Rotary Hammer is model P223, used here. 'Makita XRH011' is ambiguous between XRH01Z (18V, current) and XRH11Z (18V X2/36V, confirmed DISCONTINUED on makitatools.com); XRH01Z is used as the current, in-production model (its factory kit SKU XRH011TWX is likely the source of the seed's digit string). Milwaukee's bare 2717-20 SDS-max hammer is flagged discontinued (April 2026, SupplyHouse) and was replaced in this dataset by its current successor, 2917-20 w/ONE-KEY.

Verified 2026-08-01.

products.name: Hilti TE 6-A36-AVR 36V Cordless SDS-Plus Rotary Hammer
products.priceNote: Bare-tool price per Pro Tool Reviews; Hilti sells direct/through reps and does not publish a traditional public MSRP -- full kits with batteries, charger and dust extraction run well above this, up to roughly $1,700.
products.provenance: Pro Tool Reviews' hands-on review (which cites Hilti's own published spec sheet) gives 36V lithium-ion, 1.8 ft-lb (2.4 J) single impact energy, 5,100 BPM impact rate, 1,050 RPM no-load hammer-drilling speed, SDS-Plus (TE-C) chuck, 8.2 lb weight, four operating modes (hammering / hammering-with-rotation / rotation-only / chisel-angle mode), AVR active vibration reduction, and $449 for the bare tool vs. $1,667-$1,790 for fully loaded kits across sources. Hilti's own downloadable spec-sheet PDF (nixonhire.co.uk) could not be parsed as text (binary/corrupted extraction), so the review's transcription of Hilti's figures is used as the primary citable source instead. An optimal concrete-drilling sub-range (1/4-5/8 in.) is documented but no single 'max diameter' figure is stated, so max_drill_diameter_mm is left null rather than assumed -- unlike the inch-named Bosch/DeWalt/Makita/Ryobi/Milwaukee models, Hilti's 'TE 6' designation is a performance-class code, not a diameter code. Verified 2026-08-01.
